books.title: Weird Building Plans
books.author: Unknown
pages:
PLATE I — FURNACE

A series of
careful drawings
depicts a forge
constructed from
unusually dark
stone.

Its firebox
appears to have no
ordinary fuel

chamber. Instead,
a narrow channel
runs beneath the
structure,
connecting to an
opening at its
base.

Several
measurements have
been corrected in
red ink.

PLATE II — SECOND
APPARATUS

A low stone
platform with a
hollow centre,
surrounded by four
raised supports.

The central
opening is marked
with a strange

symbol, repeated
throughout the
remaining pages.

PLATES III–VI —
PASSAGES

Detailed
cross-sections of
tunnels, showing
precisely measured
widths and support

placements.

Some passages are
lined with timber,
while others
deliberately leave
the stone exposed.

Several routes
appear to end
without purpose.
Others curve back

toward the same
point.

One instruction is
underlined
repeatedly:

"Do not obstruct
the central
channels."

The final page

contains a complex
arrangement of
measurements, with
no explanation of
what the completed
construction is
meant to
accomplish.

books.title: A Tale of the Past
books.author: A village elder
pages:
They will tell you
that the city
beneath this
island was lost
long before our
time. That much is
true. They may
also tell you that
whatever lived
down there is long
gone. I wish that
were true as well.

I am no scholar. I
cannot tell you
what we found or
where it came
from. But I saw
what it did to
good people. We
thought we could
take what we
needed and leave
the rest alone.
We were wrong.

There is something
buried beneath
this island, and
it should remain
that way. If it
ever stirs again,
do not be tempted
by the gifts it
seems to offer. No
matter how
wonderful they may
appear, they are

not worth the
price. Seal it
away. Better yet,
destroy it, if
such a thing is
possible.

And tell your
children. Make
sure they tell
theirs.
I do not care if

they believe this
tale.

I only pray they
remember it.

books.title: Research Journal I
books.author: Unknown researcher
pages:
We have finally
reached what
appears to be the
remains of an
ancient city,
buried deep
beneath the
island. Much of
its architecture
has already
collapsed or been
swallowed by the

surrounding earth.
The surviving
structures suggest
a remarkable
degree of
planning, though
their original
purpose remains
unclear.

Among the rubble,
we discovered

several fragments
of a strange
material. The
workers have taken
to calling them
"Echo Shards."
Despite their
delicate
appearance, their
edges are
remarkably sharp.
Their peculiar

properties warrant
further
examination. I
have collected a
number of
specimens for
experimentation.
Perhaps they may
prove useful
beyond their
apparent purpose
as decorative

remnants.

There is still
much to uncover
here. I suspect we
have only
scratched the
surface of what
this place once
was.

books.title: Research Journal II
books.author: Unknown researcher
pages:
A most peculiar
discovery.

A dark,
mycelium-like
substance appears
to permeate many
of the ancient
pathways. At
first, we assumed
it to be some form
of subterranean

fungus, although
its unusual
appearance
suggests
otherwise. Several
of the pathways
have collapsed,
and wherever their
boundaries were
broken, the growth
has spread into
the surrounding

stone. During our
repairs, we
noticed something
rather curious:
planks seem to
halt its advance,
whereas ordinary
stone is readily
overtaken. This
may explain the
peculiar
construction of

the ancient
passages. Further
observation is
necessary.

We have also
uncovered deposits
of a striking
violet crystal.
The material
appears remarkably
durable, resisting

several of our
attempts to work
it. I have marked
its location for
future study.

Between these
crystals, the
strange growth,
and the Echo
Shards, I am
beginning to

suspect the
ancients possessed
knowledge we have
yet to rediscover.

books.title: Research Journal III
books.author: Unknown researcher
pages:
A breakthrough!

Using the dark
stone recovered
from the ruins, we
have successfully
reconstructed what
appears to be a
form of ancient
forge. Curiously,
the apparatus
refuses to ignite

using conventional
fuels. Neither
coal nor charcoal
produces any
meaningful
reaction. However,
when brought into
contact with the
strange growth we
have begun
referring to as
"sculk," the forge

becomes active.
How it draws
energy from this
substance remains
a mystery.

For the time
being, we have
decided to keep
our discoveries
from the residents
above. Rumours of

strange growths
and ancient
machinery would
undoubtedly cause
unnecessary alarm.

Initial
experiments have
been remarkably
promising. Rather
than merely
heating materials,

the forge appears
capable of
improving existing
equipment. I
intend to
investigate its
interaction with
the other
substances
recovered from the
city. In
particular, I am

curious what
effect those
peculiar sea-green
shards might
produce.

The possibilities
are quite
extraordinary.

books.title: Research Journal IV
books.author: Unknown researcher
pages:
We have begun
recreating the
passages observed
in the ancient
city, deliberately
allowing the sculk
to spread along
predetermined
routes.

In theory, this
should permit us

to harness its
properties without
exposing the
surrounding mine.
Our first attempt
was, admittedly,
less successful
than anticipated.

The growth escaped
through a poorly
secured section

and rapidly
overtook the
neighbouring
stonework. It
required
considerable
effort to remove,
but I am confident
that we have
eliminated the
unwanted growth.
The sheer quantity

of timber and
stone required for
these
constructions has
begun attracting
attention from the
villagers above.
We must be more
discreet.

We have also
relocated the

forge to the ridge
overlooking the
city. The
environment below
has become
increasingly
unpleasant, and
the elevated
location offers a
more suitable
workspace. Further
experiments have

confirmed that the
forge responds to
finished equipment
rather than raw
materials such as
ingots. Even
mundane substances
can produce
unexpected
results. Flint,
for instance,
appears to enhance

the effectiveness
of a bow.

Such discoveries
only reinforce my
conviction that
our work is
worthwhile.

With improved
containment, I see
no reason we

cannot continue
safely.

books.title: Research Journal V
books.author: Unknown researcher
pages:
Our efforts have
yielded another
extraordinary
discovery.

We have
successfully
reconstructed a
second apparatus.
For lack of a
better term, I
have taken to

calling it the
"Altar."

Unlike the forge,
this device
appears to act
upon the
individual who
approaches it.
Those who offer
themselves to its
strange ritual

report
experiencing
abilities beyond
their ordinary
capabilities.

There is, however,
a cost. Its
precise nature
remains uncertain,
though I believe
further

experimentation
will reveal the
underlying
mechanism.

Interestingly, the
forge and altar
interfere with one
another when
positioned too
closely.
We have therefore

relocated the
altar to the small
research chamber
within the mine,
necessitating a
further expansion
of our sculk
network.

Containment
continues to
present

difficulties. The
growth seems to
exploit every
opening, no matter
how insignificant.

Nevertheless, a
simple hoe is
remarkably
effective at
removing it. A
manageable

inconvenience, all
things considered.

Of greater
interest are the
peculiar
formations
emerging among the
sculk.

Some respond to
movement, almost

as though
listening. Others
produce an awful
shrieking sound
when disturbed.
When the
neighbouring
growths are
triggered, a deep,
rhythmic pulse can
sometimes be
heard.

It is strangely
reminiscent of a
heartbeat.

I have instructed
the workers to
exercise caution
around these
formations until
we understand
their purpose.
On a more

encouraging note,
a simple feather
has produced
remarkable results
when used with the
forge. My boots
now possess an
extraordinary
lightness that is
difficult to
describe.
Every experiment

brings another
discovery.

It would be
foolish to turn
back now.

books.title: Research Journal VI
books.author: Unknown researcher
pages:
Today, we ventured
into the heart of
the ancient city
for the first time
in some weeks.

The sculk has
spread
considerably
further than our
previous estimates
suggested. Entire

passages are now
covered, and the
shrieking
formations have
become
distressingly
numerous.
Nevertheless, we
pressed onward,
hoping to examine
the structure we
have come to call

the "Heart."

After the third
shriek, something
extraordinary
occurred. The
ground itself
seemed to come
alive, and an
enormous creature
emerged from the
sculk. We had

never encountered
anything like it.

We withdrew
immediately.
Fortunately, the
creature did not
pursue us for
long, and we
eventually watched
it burrow back
into the growth

from which it had
appeared.

For want of a
better name, I
have designated
this creature a
"Warden." Could it
be some form of
guardian? Perhaps
created to protect
the Heart?

Whatever its
purpose, its
appearance
presents a
considerable
obstacle to our
research. I have
therefore ordered
a second
expedition. We
shall clear the
affected passages,

remove the
shrieking
formations, and
establish a secure
route to the
Heart. After all,
the sculk still
requires exposed
surfaces and room
into which it can
expand. With
sufficient care,

its spread can be
contained.

The Warden is
undoubtedly
dangerous, but
danger alone is no
reason to abandon
our work. We have
achieved too much
to surrender our
discoveries now.

We must simply
regain control.

books.title: Warning for Those Who Come After
books.author: Unknown worker
books.description: Just before the Ancient Altar room; old dried blood stains
pages:
A warning for
those who come
after

If you are reading
this, I hope the
passage behind me
is still blocked.

I was only a
worker down here.
I helped build the

tunnels, carried
supplies, and
cleared away that
awful black
growth.I never
understood half of
what the
researchers were
doing.

Today, we went
down into the

heart of the city
again. We were
meant to clear the
way and remove
those things that
kept screaming at
us. At first, it
went well. Then
one of those
creatures came out
of the ground. The
Head Researcher

called them
Wardens. A name
did nothing to
save us.

It killed the
others. I ran as
fast as I could,
but I could hear
it following me,
coming up through
the passages we

had built.

We should never
have built those
passages. We had
discussed what to
do if something
went wrong. I am
going to bring
down the supports
and collapse part
of the mine. With

any luck, that
will trap the
creature below.

I don't know if it
will work.

I don't know if
I'll make it out.

But if you are
standing here now,

then you have
found the same
place we once
found. Please, be
smarter than we
were. The
researcher thought
he could control
it. We all
believed him. And
for a while, it
seemed he was

right. The forge,
the altar, all
those wonderful
things we could
suddenly do...

None of it was
worth this.

Whatever you think
you might gain
from this place,

leave it alone. If
you can, destroy
the growth before
it takes the whole
island. And
whatever you do,
don't open the way
again.

Please….
